title: Large personal MSX, Apple II, Atari ST, C64 and BBC discovery pass
summary: Personally screen 235 unique URLs from 238 search hits, review 30 roots, add 27 projects, consolidate one predecessor and defer two source-container claims.
notes: All discovery and publication performed personally by the root assistant, without a research worker, PR or new branch. Five fresh platform searches were combined with previously unreviewed Atari/C64 search candidates and screened against current main. Thirty selected roots received immutable primary-source inspection, including implementation rather than README alone. Generic Oric/microbit substring hits were triaged out and are not counted as reviewed projects. Original MSX homebrew, incomplete demonstrations, historical application source, developer tools and modern reimplementations remain distinct. Explicit hardware requirements, guessed image ordering, missing source containers, parser robustness limitations and predecessor relationships are retained. No upstream program, game, ROM, disk image or test suite was executed; source review does not independently certify build or gameplay. Pinned proof blobs were verified locally before sealing.

sources.reason: Substantial native shoot-em-up prototype with Screen11 presentation, ASCII16 mapping, scrolling, level/player logic and animation modules. Author calls it a demo/POC rather than a finished arcade port.
Native Samurai Shodown-inspired V9990 demonstration with graphics setup, palettes and animation source. The upstream description explicitly says unplayable proof of concept.
Pixel-scrolling platform game with parallax, player/enemy logic, maps and multi-colour sprite presentation. Reviewed actual jump/fall/run game logic.
Falling-block match-three puzzle game with horizontal/vertical/diagonal matches, combos, levels and keyboard/joystick input. Main C source wires title and game loops into MSX BIOS support.
Sixteen-round arcade game with direction/charge input, enemies and exits. Z80 enemy-pattern parsing and spawn control implementation inspected.
Readable BASIC paddle/ball game with explicit collision, velocity, scoring and sound code, alongside disk distribution and design documents.
BASIC action game moves floors to rescue pigs while avoiding wolves; substantial state, sprite and input routines are included.
BASIC missile-control game with scrolling asteroid rows, fuel, acceleration, target-hit checks and sound. Source includes timing adjustment for identified machine state.
Converts standard Apple II sector-image bytes into WOZ track representation and writes CRC metadata. Concrete serializer implementation inspected.
Go library/CLI reads and writes ProDOS hard-drive images, with directory, bitmap, file and BASIC handling. Actual seedling/sapling/tree file write paths inspected.
Disk-image ingestion and indexed file/sector comparisons, duplicate/subset discovery, extraction and BASIC tokenization across several Apple II filesystems. Inspected container loading source.
Browser tool parses text-grid shapes with origin markers, vectorizes and packs Applesoft shape commands, and downloads a binary shape table. Actual parse/vector assembly pipeline inspected.
Creates ROMXc/e application images that preload and launch Applesoft BASIC. Actual loader bank/ROM and BASIC-memory handling inspected.
Research scripts decode Mystery House dictionaries, messages, objects, rooms and graphics data, with captured outputs. Accompanies the authors' 2019 archaeological study.
Original commercial1993 Atari ST guitar-reference source is preserved alongside a later HTML/JavaScript adaptation. Inspected GEM/MIDI C routines and author provenance.
Parses Motorola/GAS/MIT assembly and estimates instruction/control-flow costs for 68000 through 68060. Inspected CPU model selection and instruction-size reasoning code.
PI1 display and PNG conversion with reference-palette reuse and optional contiguous16×16 tile output. Actual palette quantization/linearization implementation inspected.
Runs SNDH playback through adapted AtariAudio machinery and dumps YM2149/MFP register state for music analysis. Inspected command-line/subsong setup.
Substantial historical C/assembly and GEM resource sources for file/disk mapping, search, edit, copy and recovery operations. Root source preservation is useful despite absent README.
C64 Duck and Cover game plus two minigames, with both Lisp-like compiler inputs and generated 6502 assembly. Reviewed assembly entry and scoreboard logic.
Lisp-like arcade-game language and runtime generator emits readable 6502 assembly, with sprite definitions, collision helpers and scoreboards. Concrete emitter startup inspected.
Native 6502 port of Kaptajn Kaper i Kattegat, including trading, sailing, cannon combat, map events and help application. Assembly comments link original BASIC logic.

Reimplements Land of Spur BBS gameplay as a shared Python asyncio world with native C64/C128 clients; preserves original SPUR source and prior modBASIC work. Inspected substantial editor conversion implementation.
Native platform-engine experiment with map/sprite/IRQ routines and design notes. ACME entry file and module graph inspected.
Converts FSD disc-image tracks/sectors into FDI structures, carrying deleted-data and CRC-error flags. Actual conversion loop inspected.
Catalogues and unpacks DFS SSD images with load/execute metadata and unused-sector inspection. Actual file metadata/extraction code inspected.
MCP server and in-process Python driver control real beebjit sessions, keyboard, screen capture, RAM/registers and6502 disassembly. Inspected keycode mapping and protocol-facing translation.
Duplicate/predecessor: README explicitly says DSKalyzer was succeeded by DiskM8, promoted in this batch. Preserve lineage instead of tracking both as current independent tools.

Defer source-container inspection: author identifies this as the original1988 speaker sound editor and says its DOS3.3 disk includes machine-language source. Root exposes only disk image and article PDF; source inside the image was not verified in this pass. This is not a claim that source is absent.

Defer software-source inclusion: README describes a C++/ICBYTES recreation, but inspected recursive tree contains executable and media without C/C++ source or project build files. Do not promote documentary claims as a source-backed reconstruction.
